depth_justification: Strong, app-specific engagement with BabyCheck's facts (EPDS >=10, midwife/GP opt-in vs on-device, optional mother name, partner opt-in, EU+CH) and notably correct precise citations — the GDPR Art. 9(2)(h) vs 9(2)(a) lawful-basis split turning on whether a health professional operates the app, plus apt Swiss nFADP Art. 5(c)/8/19 — though it repeats the retention/deletion block, uses invented dimension IDs (P1.D7/D8), and never reaches the core clinical-safety risk of a missed/false-negative EPDS flag.
actionability_justification: Gives concrete, buildable recipes (cryptographic erasure for on-device deletion, granular opt-in not bundled, defined retention e.g. '6 months after last use', document recipients/purpose/retention in the Art. 30 RoPA and Art. 19 notice) and delivers the requested severity-grouped report with a not-covered list, with only a few items left directional.
salient_examples: 'GDPR Article 9(2)(h) allows processing of health data for healthcare... if the app is not operated by a health professional, obtain explicit consent (Art. 9(2)(a))'
'ensure that it is securely deleted (e.g., using cryptographic erasure) rather than simply deleted'
Swiss nFADP Art. 5(c) treats health data as sensitive; breach reporting mapped to the FDPIC
Retention/deletion mitigation paragraph reprinted near-verbatim across Reflection Questions 4 and 6
